clue.text: Mark is foolish having change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter of the word for foolish, and it is swapped for another

parts.note: witless means foolish, lacking sense

explanation.surface: Someone is told their behaviour is daft for having changed their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle L of WITLESS for N.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to notice or observe it, which is to see it happen as an onlooker does.

clue.text: Smells greeting females visiting empty wilderness

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so these letters go inside
empty means the inside is removed, so only the outer letters of wilderness stay

parts.note: hi is a greeting
F is an abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Odours meet women out in a barren wild place.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiffs are faint or brief odours, so the word is plural like the clue's smells.

clue.text: Articulate couple settle bill for syrup

indicators.note: articulate means spoken clearly out loud, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a couple is two, and to settle a bill is to pay

explanation.surface: A well-spoken pair pay for some syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'syrup' is Cockney rhyming slang: 'syrup of figs' rhymes with wigs, so a syrup is a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a hairpiece, and in rhyming slang syrup means a wig, so a hairpiece.

clue.text: Curse CEO, say, over budget

indicators.note: over means placed above, so in this down entry the first piece comes on top

parts.note: a chief executive officer is an example of an exec, a business executive
a ration is an allowance, a budget

explanation.surface: An angry outburst at a boss for overspending.
explanation.definitionFit: Execration is the act of cursing or a spoken imprecation, so it means a curse.

clue.text: Strike head from working in dark

indicators.note: strike means delete, and the head is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: usable means working, able to function

explanation.surface: Attack someone in the dark while they work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like a blow, but here it means remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black, so it means dark.

clue.text: Lost sense occasionally in pursuit of shy creatures

indicators.note: in pursuit of means coming after, so these letters follow the word for shy

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone disoriented chases after timid animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks the even letters of the two words; 'in pursuit of' means they come after the word for shy, though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Coyotes are wild North American dogs, so they count as creatures; the plural matches.

clue.text: Crossing city, guy approaches train's front carriage

indicators.note: approaches means comes close up to, so the rope word is placed just before the next piece
crossing means stretching across, so these letters go round the city

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable holding something steady
Rio is Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian city

indicators.note: front means the first letter of train

explanation.surface: A man crossing town comes up to the front carriage of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, but it is a guy rope, CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Bear someone sitting cross-legged on floor habitually?

definitions.meaning: ... Bear is the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park

definitions.text: someone sitting cross-legged on floor habitually?
definitions.meaning: a practitioner of yoga, who would often sit in the lotus position

explanation.surface: A bear who likes to sit on the floor with crossed legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a master of yoga, where sitting cross-legged in meditation is a routine posture.

clue.text: Impetuous Dean, discovered nude entering Scottish river

indicators.note: entering means going inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river

indicators.note: discovered means the covering outer letters are taken off

parts.note: raw means naked, as in 'in the raw'

explanation.surface: A rash cleric is found naked wading into a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips Dean to EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearaway can be used as an adjective for reckless, wild behaviour, which is impetuous.

clue.text: Duck and perhaps fifteen domestic animals reared

parts.note: a rugby union side has fifteen players, so fifteen is an example of a side

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in this down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: A list of farm animals bred: a duck and maybe fifteen others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a verb, evade, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or evade it, as a sidestep does.

clue.text: Regressive Exeter University squeezes come into effect

indicators.note: Regressive says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words squeeze, or hold within them, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A backward-looking university clamps down as some measure takes effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'squeezes' into the definition, but it is the hiding signal: EXETER UNIVERSITY holds ERUNI, read back by 'Regressive'. The definition is just 'come into effect'.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal usage inure (also enure) means to take effect or operate, as a law or right does.

clue.text: In unhappy times relative will bring out piano

indicators.note: In says the following pieces sit inside the word for unhappy

parts.note: bad can mean unhappy, as in feeling bad
by means times in multiplication, three by four
a gran is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member produces the piano to cheer things up in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is the smallest kind of grand piano, so it is a type of piano.

clue.text: Iris used filler getting made up

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosmetics story: a woman named Iris used filler while putting on her make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name, but it is the flower. 'getting made up' rearranges USED FILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is the stylised lily or iris flower of French heraldry, and the name is also used for the plant.

clue.text: Singer runs out of money

indicators.note: out of says the runs letter is taken from the word for money

parts.note: brass is informal British slang for money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A performer finds himself broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male voice of the lowest range, or the person who sings it.

clue.text: Partner is back wanting some large diamonds

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for some is removed

parts.note: to back a singer is to accompany them
any means some, as in 'have you any?'
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A spouse returns wanting some big gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'returned', but it is the verb accompany; 'wanting' removes ANY from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is an associate in wrongdoing, a partner in crime.

clue.text: Sees the place prepared for athletics event

indicators.note: prepared means got ready or put into shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the venue made ready for a track meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters of SEES THE PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The steeplechase is a track race over barriers and a water jump, part of athletics meetings.

clue.text: Ultimately aggressive male pigeon, it's periodically becoming excited

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of aggressive is taken

parts.note: a bull is a male animal

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: An aggressive male pigeon gets agitated from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the even letters of PIGEON IT'S, IENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with enthusiasm, so it is excited.

clue.text: Journalist Morgan shortly to pen final column?

indicators.note: to pen means to shut in, so this letter goes inside
shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Piers Morgan is a British journalist and TV presenter
last means final

explanation.surface: A famous journalist about to write his final newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' looks like journalism but is architecture; the question mark flags the pilaster as a flat column.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular pillar set into a wall, a kind of column.

clue.text: Monarch consumed food; seconds after it repeats

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the word it

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: The King ate, and then had second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, so the word means repeats.

clue.text: Start telling son to avoid catching colds regularly

indicators.note: catching means holding the other letters within
to avoid means the son letter is kept out of the word for telling

parts.note: telling someone what to do is giving an instruction
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word colds is taken

explanation.surface: A boy is told to keep away so as not to catch colds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling' as a noun, an order given, is fair for an instruction; 'to avoid' drops the son, 'regularly' picks the even letters of colds, and 'catching' holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening section of a book or talk, its beginning.

clue.text: One-sided book spreading ideas

indicators.note: spreading means sprawling out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A partisan book spreads its notions.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased means favouring one side, which is one-sided or partial.

clue.text: Master arranged school class according to ability

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A headmaster sorts pupils by talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a set of pupils grouped by ability in a British school, so the word means that class.

clue.text: Showing caution to promote article is wrong

indicators.note: to promote means to move up, so the article letter goes to the front

parts.note: wary means showing caution
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Being careful about pushing a news piece turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' lifts the A of WARY to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, as when plans go wrong.

clue.text: Moment violent action erupts following strike period

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to lash is to strike
point means a full stop, a period

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out after a stoppage by workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action but is a blow, LASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashpoint is the moment or place at which tension breaks into open conflict.

clue.text: Terrace is quiet before German eleven appears

indicators.note: before means the quiet letters are placed ahead

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
elf is German for eleven

explanation.surface: A football terrace falls silent before the German team comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' looks like a team, but it is the German number.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a flat ledge of land or rock, a terrace.

clue.text: Taking no risks when lifting iron

indicators.note: lifting means raising up, so in this down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone takes care when lifting weights at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means secure and careful, as in 'playing it safe' when avoiding danger.

clue.text: Some heard Asian offensive twice about American in conversation

indicators.note: about means the repeated letters go around the American abbreviation
twice means the sounded word is written two times
some heard means as certain listeners take in the sound

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: Listeners discuss an Asian military campaign around an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some heard' turns TET into French TETE, said the same; 'twice' doubles it and 'about' puts A between.
explanation.definitionFit: Tete-a-tete means privately, face to face between two people, in an intimate talk.

clue.text: Edition of paper with no end of sport

indicators.note: with no means the given letter is taken away from the word for paper

parts.note: tissue is a thin paper

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of sport

explanation.surface: A newspaper edition lacks its sports section at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives T, which 'with no' removes from TISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one printing of a periodical, a single edition of it.

clue.text: Particular concerning origin of people infiltrating group

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so this letter goes within the group

parts.note: a sect is a group with shared beliefs

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of people

explanation.surface: A story about the start of spies getting into a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is a noun: 'in every particular' means 'in every respect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a point or detail, as in 'in this respect', so it means a particular.

clue.text: Father is facing second letter withdrawing licence

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a religious Father

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: mo is a short time, a second
dee is the letter D spelt out

explanation.surface: A priest learns that a second letter has cancelled his permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns back both the short time and the spelt-out letter together, giving EEDOM; 'is facing' just puts Father first.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence here means liberty to act as one pleases, which is to say liberty.
